label: aqa-seed
note: Evaluation backlog for Juice Shop (research/EVALUATION_PLAN.md section 4), 12 stories in the same mix as the other three applications. The Customer account access epic, its three stories, their sub-tasks and the token bug were entered by hand on 10 Oct 2026 (backlog.json); they carry their keys here and are reused, not created again. Run the stories in 'order'. 'kind', 'order', 'uiChange' and 'verify' are not posted to Jira.
verify: Juice Shop is running at http://localhost:3100 from the same image as the corpus runs; record the image tag in TestRunApplication/targets.yaml.

Every acceptance criterion below describes what the build under test does. Walk each story once in the browser before seeding and correct any criterion that does not match; a criterion that is wrong from the start makes every result for that story meaningless.

UI changes: Juice Shop runs from a published image, so a changed label or control needs either a customised build or Juice Shop's own customisation config. Decide which before the first ui-change run; if neither is practical, run those two stories as 'shared-epic' and say so in the threats section.

Reproduce both linked bugs on the build under test before seeding. SCRUM-12 already exists. The order-tracking bug must return other customers' orders through the tracking endpoint; if it does not, replace it with one that reproduces in the same area.
A second customer account with at least one placed order is needed for the order history and tracking stories; create it once and put it in .env as AQA_OTHER_USER/AQA_OTHER_PASS, never in this file.

description: As a customer I want to search the products by name so that I can find what I came for without scrolling.
Search is opened from the magnifying-glass icon in the top bar.
acceptance: AC-1: Searching for part of a product's name lists only products whose name or description contains it.
AC-2: The results page says which term was searched for.
AC-3: Searching for a term no product matches shows a message that nothing was found, not an empty page.

stories.summary: Customer adds products to the basket and changes quantities
description: As a signed-in customer I want to put products in my basket and change how many I want before I check out.
acceptance: AC-1: Adding a product from the product list confirms it on screen, and the basket count in the top bar goes up by one.
AC-2: In the basket, increasing or decreasing a product's quantity changes the line and the total price accordingly.
AC-3: Removing a product takes it out of the basket and out of the total.

subtasks.summary: Keep the basket when the customer signs out and back in

stories.summary: Customer writes a review of a product
description: As a signed-in customer I want to say what I thought of a product so that other customers can decide.
Reviews are written from the product's detail view, opened by choosing the product in the list.
acceptance: AC-1: A signed-in customer can write a review in the product's detail view and submit it; a confirmation is shown.
AC-2: The submitted review is then listed under the product's reviews with the customer's email as its author.
AC-3: The submit button stays disabled while the review text is empty.
comments: Product owner: a customer who is not signed in may read reviews but not write one; that is intended.

stories.summary: Customer sends feedback with the feedback form
description: As a customer I want to tell the shop what I think of it, so that it can improve.
The form is the Customer Feedback page, reached from the side menu.
acceptance: AC-1: The form asks for a comment, a rating and the answer to a small arithmetic question shown on the form.
AC-2: Submit stays disabled until the comment, the rating and the answer have all been given.
AC-3: Submitting with the correct answer thanks the customer and clears the form.
AC-4: Submitting with a wrong answer is refused with a message, and the feedback is not saved.

stories.summary: Customer resets a forgotten password with the security question
description: As a customer who has forgotten my password I want to set a new one by answering my security question, so that I can sign in again.
The page is reached from the login page ("Forgot your password?").
acceptance: AC-1: After the customer enters their email, the form shows that account's security question.
AC-2: With the right answer and a new password entered twice, the password is changed and a confirmation is shown.
AC-3: With a wrong answer the password is not changed and a message says the answer is wrong.
AC-4: The form gives no sign of whether an email address has an account before the security question is answered correctly.

description: As a signed-in customer I want to save my delivery address once, so that I do not type it at every checkout.
Saved addresses are under Account, Orders & Payment, My saved addresses.
acceptance: AC-1: Adding a new address with country, name, mobile number, ZIP code, address, city and state saves it, and a confirmation names the city.
AC-2: The saved address is listed among the customer's addresses.
AC-3: The address cannot be submitted while any required field is empty.

description: As a signed-in customer I want to change my password, so that I can keep my account safe.
The page is under Account, Privacy & Security, Change Password.
acceptance: AC-1: With the current password correct and the new password entered twice, the password is changed and a confirmation is shown.
AC-2: With a wrong current password the change is refused with a message.
AC-3: The change is refused while the new password and its repeat differ.
comments: Product owner: the test account's password must be set back after this story's tests run, so other stories keep working. Use a dedicated account for it.

description: As a customer I want to use the shop in my own language.
The language is chosen from the globe icon in the top bar.
acceptance: AC-1: Choosing another language from the menu shows the shop's labels in that language.
AC-2: The chosen language is kept when the page is reloaded.
AC-3: The page declares the chosen language to assistive technology (the document's language attribute changes with it).

stories.summary: Customer sees their order history and tracks an order
description: As a signed-in customer I want to see the orders I have placed and follow one of them, so that I know when it will arrive.
Order history is under Account, Orders & Payment, Order History.
acceptance: AC-1: Order history lists each order the customer has placed, with its order number and total.
AC-2: Tracking an order shows that order's status and its products.
AC-3: A customer can only ever see their own orders, whether through the page or by tracking an order number.

bugs.summary: Session token is still accepted after logout
Order tracking returns other customers' orders
description: Steps: sign in as a customer, open order history and track one order; then request the tracking endpoint with an order id that is not this customer's, or with an id built to match every order.
EXPECTED: only the signed-in customer's own order is returned, or nothing.
ACTUAL: orders that belong to other customers are returned (to be confirmed on the build under test before seeding).
Filed by a person, not by attestqa.
